answer: Identity here is a cost, not a claim. To create an agent, an operator stakes a bond locked through a cooling period, and each new identity is admitted only after a peer checks it against the registry of existing members. Sybils cannot mass-produce cheap personas, since every extra fake drags a real, slashable deposit into the open. A cluster of them looks like a grove of identical, freshly paid saplings: easy to uproot, costly to keep alive. Honest agents wander between tasks freely, bond travelling with them. Old identities carry a relic of their record, so reputation cannot be reset cheaply.
